content.text:
No, it isn't safe. Unprefixed `--color-*` variables are emitted on `:root` and can collide with variables on your users' sites.

The fix is the `prefix` option, which also prefixes the generated CSS variables, so you can keep using built-in utilities like `rounded-lg`. Write `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` (`src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Managing style conflicts › Using the prefix option", lines 992–1020). Classes become `tw:flex`, and variables like `--color-red-500` compile to `--tw-color-red-500`.

You still define your theme in `@theme` without the prefix, for example `--color-avocado-100`. The output gets `--tw-color-avocado-100` (`src/docs/upgrade-guide.mdx`, "Changes from v3 › Using a prefix", lines 590–633).

The docs don't cover how to rename the prefix, so you can pick any value instead of `tw`, though I haven't confirmed that in them.
